title: PUFiM: A Robust and Efficient FeFET-Based Security Solution Merging Physical Unclonable Function with Compute-in-Memory for Edge AI
problem: CiM architectures for edge AI leak model weights stored in plaintext; while PUFs could provide key generation, existing approaches lack comprehensive key generation/delivery frameworks and incur high storage overhead for ciphertext.
motivation: CiM is attractive for edge deployment due to reduced data movement, but security-critical edge AI applications need on-chip key generation and encrypted computation without excessive overhead.
method: PUFiM integrates ferroelectric FET (FeFET) PUFs with CiM arrays in unified architecture using multi-level cell (MLC) FeFETs for hybrid PUF+weight storage. Combines three innovations: (1) strong PUF co-designed with CiM for key generation and authentication; (2) high-density hybrid storage via MLC FeFETs avoiding separate ciphertext storage; (3) PUF enhancement techniques and novel mapping scheme for improved robustness.
key_novelty: First work synergizing physical unclonable functions with CiM in unified array for end-to-end security without ciphertext storage overhead.
contributions: Withstands PUF modeling attacks with up to 10M samples
9.7x compute density improvement vs. SRAM/NVM secure CiMs
1.2x energy efficiency improvement while maintaining >60% accuracy under 95% key leakage

metrics.other: compute density 9.7x, energy efficiency 1.2x, attack resilience to 10M samples

limitations: Not discussed; applicability to larger models and quantitative accuracy numbers under various attack scenarios unclear.
primary_theme: FeFET-based unified PUF and compute-in-memory for edge AI security
